findings.description: Cell protection: EARS requirement states 'shall protect the cell against manual edits', A-outputs implement ProtectedRange with warning_only:false across all three variants, B-outputs omit any mention of protection (correctly reflecting code absence), and real code at sheets-view/src/lib.rs contains zero ProtectedRange API calls. This is a spec-to-code gap visible bidirectionally: the requirement is explicit in the EARS text, A-side correctly reads and implements it, B-side correctly identifies its absence from the implementation.

Decimal precision: A-outputs variously specify 0 decimals (A2, rounded integer), 2 decimals (A3), or variable precision (A1); B-outputs unanimously identify exactly 4 decimals; real code at lib.rs line 504 formats as '{frac:04}%' confirming exactly 4 decimals (e.g., Ppm(150_000) → '15.0000%'). A-side is uniformly wrong; B-side correctly identified code precision.

Input domain divergence: A1 invents [0.0, 100.0] percent-scale input (e.g., 25.5 → '25.5%'), A2/A3 invent [0.0, 1.0] decimal-scale input with clamping; spec does not specify input domain. B-outputs correctly identify Ppm type (parts per million, signed i64) from config crate; real code uses Ppm throughout and delegates validation to tax crate. A1's 0-100 scale is incompatible with the effective-rate semantics (which are 0-1 fractions); all A-outputs invented a domain not present in spec.

A2 violates spec's encoding channel: EARS specifies 'percent-typed userEnteredValue'; A2 alone uses stringValue with PERCENT numberFormat instead of the mandated userEnteredValue, contradicting both spec and code (which implements Cell::Value → userEnteredValue per line 439-445).

A2 invents numberFormat specification: A2 specifies explicit CellFormat with numberFormat type 'PERCENT' and pattern '0%', neither of which appear in the EARS spec or in the real code (which relies on Sheets parsing the '%-suffixed userEnteredValue string without setting numberFormat).
